newsitem.title: UK: Hanging adds macabre twist to British murder saga.
newsitem.headline: Hanging adds macabre twist to British murder saga.

text.p: The terrible saga of Britain's West family, whose lifestyle was grotesquely exposed by the "House of Horrors" murder trial, took a macabre, final twist on Friday with the apparent suicide of John West.

West, 54, was found hanging from a beam in the garage of his home near Abbeymead, western England, three miles (5 km) from the former home of his evil elder brother Fred -- a building so notorious that officials not only knocked it down but ground its bricks into dust.

West was awaiting a jury's verdict on charges he had raped his niece Anne Marie Davis at 25 Cromwell Street, Gloucester, where Fred and Fred's wife Rosemary raped, tortured and murdered girls and young women.

Anne Marie, who had been abused by Fred and who was a key witness in last year's trial of Rosemary, claimed John West had raped her 300 times, starting when she was just 10 years old. John had pleaded not guilty to the charges.
His final moments mirrored the death of Fred, who hanged himself in jail on New Year's Day 1995 while awaiting trial on charges of murdering 12 women and girls.
Rosemary is now serving 10 life sentences for murdering girls and young women. Many of their bodies were found buried in the garden and cellar at 25 Cromwell Street.
The surviving West brother, Doug, said: "It is unbelievable that John has done this, just like Fred did. We have spent the last two years trying to rebuild our lives and now this."

The death of the tall, bearded John West was "another tragedy in what seems to be an endless sequence of sad events" first uncovered when the bodies were found in Fred and Rosemary's home, Detective Superintendent John Bennett told a news conference.

Davis, 32, had figured prominently in the trial of her stepmother Rosemary, testifying that she had been forcibly raped by her father Fred at the age of nine. "It hurt so much I wanted to die," she told the court. "I was told I should be grateful."

Davis said she been sexually abused so often by her parents that she had no idea that what her uncle was doing was wrong. Her uncle, who double-dated and shared a car with Fred as a teenager, was a frequent visitor to the Wests' home.
John West had denied all charges of raping Davis and another woman, who was not named. His defence had presented other family members who said the twice-married grandfather was kindly.
"I felt safe with him. Uncle John was always known as a gentle giant," Lorna Gatfield, another niece, told the court:
The jury had been due to start its deliberations on Friday. West faced a life sentence if convicted.
Another shadow hung over West's head. Before he died, Fred had accused his younger brother of helping in 20 other murders.
Bennett, who led the murder probe, said inquiries were still going on into these alleged killings "but it would not be right for me to comment on those for operational reasons".

Fred West's son Stephen said he hoped his uncle's death meant the end of the family's torment. "I hope it is, but it seems to be a never-ending story at the moment and it just goes from bad to worse," he told reporters.
"I believe it is clear he has taken his own life and I believe he knew that the odds were stacked against him and there was no way he would get out of this one."
He claimed his uncle and father had taken the easy way out, leaving his mother Rosemary to pay for their crimes.
"They have escaped justice by taking their lives."
